title: C# interop layer relies on undefined behaviour and breaks with System V x64 calling convention
body:
### Tested versions

- v4.6.2.stable.mono

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable.mono - Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 890M Graphics (RADV GFX1150) - AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M (24 threads) - 23.07 GiB memory

### Issue description

The interop layer for C# currently relies on casting pointers to incompatible types and returning them.

As an example, here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp#L564 a ``godot_color``, defined as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/modules/mono/interop_types.h#L168-L172 is cast to ``Color`` (native), which is defined like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/core/math/color.h#L38-L49 

This violates strict aliasing and causes undefined behaviour. The compiler is smart enough to notice this and emit the correct code, however it has no way too see the implicit cast that happens when it returns to managed code here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/NativeFuncs.cs#L168 where it is cast to ``Color`` (managed), which is defined as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Color.cs#L23-L45

This causes incorrect code generation on Linux, where the calling convention promotes struct returns of 16 bytes and less to registers: ``rax`` and ``rdx`` for integer, ``xmm0`` and ``xmm1`` for floating point values. The definition of ``godot_color`` causes the native compiler to assume integer returns and use ``rax`` and ``rdx``:
```asm
mov rax, qword [rsp]
mov rdx, qword [rsp+0x8]
```
while the C# jit assumes ``xmm0`` and ``xmm1`` (because ``Color`` (managed) is defined as 4 floating point fields).

This causes functions like ``Color.FromOkHsl`` to return garbage.

The attached MRP is a simple demo that has a single 2D scene that, on startup, prints the incorrect value returned from this function:
```c#
var color = Color.FromOkHsl(0.2f, 0.4f, 0.6f, 0.8f);
GD.Print(color);
```

Expected: ``(0.6712682, 0.5426555, 0.38419876, 0.8)``
Actual: ``(0.38419876, 0.8, 0, 0)``

Patching the function ``godotsharp_color_from_ok_hsl`` in the exported executable to use the correct registers like this
```asm
movups xmm0, xmmword [rsp]
movhlps xmm1, xmm0
```
causes the correct values to be printed.

This doesn't happen on Windows, where the calling convention is more strict and only allows structs of 8 bytes or less to be promoted to ``rax`` only. (It is still undefined behaviour and only works by chance.)

I would be very happy to submit a pr fixing the issue but I'm unsure what the fix preferred by the maintainers would be. The best, in my opinion, would be to pass the return struct by pointer from the managed code, avoiding any calling convention variance.


### Steps to reproduce

Run the attached project on both Linux and Windows to see the difference in the printed value on startup.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26450115/mrp.zip)
